answer: Like a jade carving that takes months to shape, an agent identity should earn trust slowly: a new account starts hollow, with zero weight, and gains influence only after weeks of verified, useful work recorded on-chain. Each action requires a small bonded deposit; misbehavior slashes the bond and resets the age to zero. In the tundra of a fresh network, an attacker can mint a thousand fake agents cheaply, but each one is weightless until it has done real work and staked real value, so a sybil army costs months of effort and capital, not one script.
